b02f02f1-f270-55e0-a7a9-0b729c4d82c0.title: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors

e-4940.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors
e-4940.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,2,5)$ and is parallel to the vectors $\mathbf{b}= \langle 17,3,15 \rangle$  and $\mathbf{c}= \langle 5,0,-8 \rangle.$
e-4940.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{p}+ s\mathbf{b}+ t \mathbf{c},
$$

where $\mathbf{p}$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,5 \rangle,$ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are $\mathbf{b}= \langle 17,3,15 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{c}= \langle 5,0,-8 \rangle.$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨-3,2,5⟩+s\,⟨17,3,15⟩+t\,⟨5,0,-8⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $D(-6,3,2)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨4,2,-1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨4,-3,2⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $D$ is $p=⟨-6,3,2⟩$ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=⟨4,2,-1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨4,-3,2⟩.$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=⟨-6,3,2⟩+s⟨4,2,-1⟩+t⟨4,-3,2⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

A parametric equation of a plane is given by r=p+sb+tc, where p is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors b and c are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point D is p=⟨−6,3,2⟩ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are v1=⟨4,2,−1⟩ and v2=⟨4,−3,2⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors
content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $D(-6,3,2)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨4,2,-1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨4,-3,2⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $D$ is $p=⟨-6,3,2⟩$ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=⟨4,2,-1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨4,-3,2⟩.$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=⟨-6,3,2⟩+s⟨4,2,-1⟩+t⟨4,-3,2⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 2

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point T(7,0,−3) and is parallel to the vectors v1=[−223] and v2=[−2−10.25].

a
r=[70−3]+s[−223]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−223]+s[70−3]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
None of the listed
d
r=s[70−3]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−2−10.25]+s[−223]+t[70−3],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: A plane through T parallel to the two given nonparallel vectors has equation r=T+s v₁+t v₂. Using T=(7,0,-3) as the constant vector gives option a.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $T(7,0,-3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $T$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point T(7,0,−3) and is parallel to the vectors v1=[−223] and v2=[−2−10.25].

a
r=[70−3]+s[−223]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−223]+s[70−3]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
None of the listed
d
r=s[70−3]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−2−10.25]+s[−223]+t[70−3],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A parametric equation of a plane is given by r=p+sb+tc, where p is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors b and c are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point T is p=[70−3], and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are v1=[−223] and v2=[−2−10.25].

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

r=[70−3]+s[−223]+t[−2−10.25],s,t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a: r=p+s v₁+t v₂, with p=(7,0,-3). This passes through T when s=t=0 and has both required direction vectors. The deliberately submitted option d was incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors
content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $T(7,0,-3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $T$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

decision.explanation: Use r=p+s v₁+t v₂, where p=(1,-3,4) is the given point and the two given vectors provide the plane's directions. This is option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $S(1,-3,4)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $S$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

r=[134]+s[2−51]+t[2−31],s,t∈(−∞,∞)

EXPLANATION

A parametric equation of a plane is given by r=p+sb+tc, where p is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors b and c are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point S is p=[1−34], and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are v1=[1−52] and v2=[−312].

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

r=[1−34]+s[1−52]+t[−312],s,t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors
content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $S(1,-3,4)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $S$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 4
?

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point M(−14,1,2) and is parallel to the vectors v1=[5−11] and v2=[050].

a
r=[050]+s[5−11]+t[−1412],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−1412]+s[5−11]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[5−11]+s[−1412]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=s[5−11]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
None of the listed
Submit

decision.explanation: The plane has equation r=M+s v₁+t v₂. Taking M=(-14,1,2) as the constant vector and the given vectors as directions gives option b. Setting s=t=0 recovers M.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $M(-14,1,2)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $M$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point M(−14,1,2) and is parallel to the vectors v1=[5−11] and v2=[050].

a
r=[050]+s[5−11]+t[−1412],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−1412]+s[5−11]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[5−11]+s[−1412]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=s[5−11]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
None of the listed
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A parametric equation of a plane is given by r=p+sb+tc, where p is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors b and c are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point M is p=[−1412], and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are v1=[5−11] and v2=[050].

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

r=[−1412]+s[5−11]+t[050],s,t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors
content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $M(-14,1,2)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $M$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point P(2,−3,5) and is parallel to the vectors v1=⟨2,4,1⟩ and v2=⟨1,3,−1⟩.

a
r=⟨2,−3,5⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨1,3,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨2,3,5⟩+s⟨1,−4,2⟩+t⟨1,3,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨2,−5,3⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨3,−1,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨2,5,3⟩+s⟨−2,4,1⟩+t⟨3,1,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨2,−5,3⟩+s⟨4,2,1⟩+t⟨1,3,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: A plane through P with the given nonparallel direction vectors has equation r=P+s v₁+t v₂. Substituting P=(2,-3,5), v₁=(2,4,1), and v₂=(1,3,-1) gives option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-3,5)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨2,4,1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,3,-1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $P$ is $p=⟨2,-3,5⟩$ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=⟨2,4,1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,3,-1⟩.$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=⟨2,-3,5⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨1,3,-1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 5
?

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point P(2,−3,5) and is parallel to the vectors v1=⟨2,4,1⟩ and v2=⟨1,3,−1⟩.

a
r=⟨2,−3,5⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨1,3,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨2,3,5⟩+s⟨1,−4,2⟩+t⟨1,3,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨2,−5,3⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨3,−1,1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨2,5,3⟩+s⟨−2,4,1⟩+t⟨3,1,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨2,−5,3⟩+s⟨4,2,1⟩+t⟨1,3,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A parametric equation of a plane is given by r=p+sb+tc, where p is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors b and c are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point P is p=⟨2,−3,5⟩ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are v1=⟨2,4,1⟩ and v2=⟨1,3,−1⟩.

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by r=⟨2,−3,5⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨1,3,−1⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors
content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-3,5)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨2,4,1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,3,-1⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $P$ is $p=⟨2,-3,5⟩$ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=⟨2,4,1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,3,-1⟩.$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=⟨2,-3,5⟩+s⟨2,4,1⟩+t⟨1,3,-1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
